learning: Iteration 0 showed off_track endings with low oscillation and 1 to 2 line-loss events, so the limit is sensor coverage and turn authority, not gain. Check whether line_loss_events falls. If it does and progress still stays low, raise kp in the next iteration. If line_loss_events stays at 1 or more, the pitch alone is not enough.
notes: Applies the Builder's 15 mm pitch and 0.10 m track with 0.7 kg mass, keeping controller gains and weights unchanged so the geometry change is isolated. Expected to reduce line-loss events and max_error, based on iteration 0's steady drift to the 0.06 m limit.
rationale: Iteration 0 (entityR2A/entityR2B) ended off_track in all 60 trials on oval, s-bend and slalom, with progress 0.10 to 0.18 and steering_oscillation of only 0.07 to 0.16. The robot is not jittering. It drifts steadily away from the line and loses it, with max_error about 0.061 to 0.066 m, right at the 0.06 m off-track limit, and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. The 5-sensor bar at 10 mm pitch spans only ±0.02 m, so all sensors go dark at a tape-centre offset of roughly 0.045 m, leaving almost no recovery margin. I follow the Builder's proposed fix in this iteration and widen the pitch to 15 mm (x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, ±0.03 m span). I also narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, which raises yaw per unit PWM by about 1.2x, and lower mass to 0.7 kg to reduce yaw inertia. The sensor weights stay at [-2,-1,0,1,2], the same as iteration 0, so the signal scale is unchanged and the geometry change is the only change in signal coverage. Gains stay at kp 1.2, ki 0.05, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.6 and line_loss last_direction, so the next race isolates the geometry change. The extra yaw authority from the narrower track partly offsets the drift, so I do not raise kp yet. Expected: fewer line_loss_events and lower max_error. If progress stays low while off_track endings persist, the next step is to raise kp or lower the forward offset, not to change the sensor pitch again. I make no claim about the outcome of this design.
